exercises.title: Which test binds on Birchwood?
exercises.intro: Run every sizing test, keep each at full precision, then take the lowest and round down to the nearest $1,000 (F-CORE-19, CORE-PRC-05).

buildup.context: Birchwood Plaza, RD-COM-01. At closing, the bridge commitment is $3,520,000 on a total cost of $5,180,000; the COM-BR LTC limit is 70%. At month 24, the term loan (F-COM-08) uses an as-stabilized value of $6,000,000 and NCF of $434,000. Its limits are 65% LTV, 1.30x DSCR and 9.0% debt yield. Annual debt service on $3,900,000 at 7.00% over 25 years is $330,772.68 (C3).

lines.label: Bridge LTC cap: 70% × total cost (F-CORE-15). Does the $3,520,000 commitment pass?
lines.hint: 70% × $5,180,000. The commitment is below it, so LTC passes.

lines.label: Term loan by LTV: 65% × as-stabilized value (F-CORE-14)
Loan constant K = ADS ÷ loan, to six decimals (F-CORE-04)
lines.hint: $330,772.68 ÷ $3,900,000. Keep the full value for the next line.

lines.label: Term loan by DSCR: NCF ÷ 1.30 ÷ K, using the unrounded K (F-CORE-17)
Term loan by debt yield: NCF ÷ 9.0% (F-CORE-18)
Final term loan: the lowest test, rounded down to the nearest $1,000 (F-CORE-19)
lines.hint: The lowest of the three is the LTV test, already a $1,000 multiple. LTV binds.

exercises.title: Build the note rate
exercises.intro: The RTL note rate is the tier base rate plus every adjuster that applies, kept within 8.50%-12.75% (F-CORE-28, CORE-PRC-02).

calculator.task: Price Maple Run. Dana Reyes is Tier 2 with a 712 mid-score. LTC is 85.0%, at the 85% maximum, and the project is a rehab. What is the note rate? Then try quiz A's flip: Tier 1, mid-score 690, LTC at the maximum.

exercises.title: Resize Maple Run's refinance
exercises.intro: Size Maple Run's month-14 refinance into a DSCR rental loan, name the binding test, and set reserves.

scenario.case: Month 14 (RD-RES-01). The appraised value is $520,000. The lease is $3,200 a month; the 1007 market rent is $3,100. Dana Reyes's mid-score is 712, and this is a rate-term refinance. Payoff is $340,000 plus about $7,000 of costs, so she asks for $347,000. Taxes are $520 and insurance $160 a month. The DSCR grid prices 7.75% above 65% LTV and 7.50% at 65% or less (RES-DSCR-12). Monthly P&I constants: 0.0071641225 at 7.75% and 0.0069921451 at 7.50%, both 30-year.
scenario.prompt: Does $347,000 pass? If not, what is the largest loan, which test binds, and how much cash must Dana bring, including reserves?
scenario.model_answer: Qualifying rent is the lesser of $3,200 and $3,100: $3,100 (RES-DSCR-01). Max LTV is 70% × $520,000 = $364,000 (RES-DSCR-03), so LTV does not bind. At $347,000 (66.7% LTV, 7.75%), PITIA = $347,000 × 0.0071641225 + $680 = $3,165.95. DSCR = $3,100 ÷ $3,165.95 = 0.98x, below 1.00x (RES-DSCR-02): fails. DSCR binds. Max by DSCR at 7.75% (F-RES-17) = ($3,100 − $680) ÷ 0.0071641225 = $337,794, or 64.96% LTV. At 65% LTV or less the rate falls to 7.50%. So the loan can rise to the 65% band edge: $338,000, a $1,000 multiple (CORE-PRC-05). Check: $338,000 × 0.0069921451 + $680 = $3,043.35; $3,100 ÷ $3,043.35 = 1.02x: passes. Dana brings $347,000 − $338,000 = $9,000 to close. Reserves are 3 × $3,043.35 = $9,130.05, shown as $9,130 (RES-DSCR-08). Her $90,900 liquidity covers both.
rubric: Uses the lesser of lease and market rent: $3,100 (RES-DSCR-01)
Uses PITIA, not P&I alone, and the unrounded constant: $3,165.95 and 0.98x at $347,000
Names DSCR as the binding test and finds $337,794 at 7.75% (F-RES-17)
Sees the 7.50% rate at 65% LTV or less and lands on $338,000, checked at 1.02x
States $9,000 cash to close plus $9,130 of reserves (RES-DSCR-08)
